$comment: Recorded by tools/capture from a real browser. Do not hand-edit the js block:
a plausible-looking value that was never measured is exactly what detection
The tls and http2 blocks are NOT recordings — the transport layer is not
observable from inside a browser. Helix presents wreq-util emulation for
this identity; these values document what that is expected to be and give
the Rust validator something to check the user-agent against.

tls.$comment: Documentation only. The handshake actually sent is wreq-util’s.

http2.$comment: chrome sends 65536; the validator rejects anything else for this engine.

headers.userAgent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/148.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
headers.$comment: Header ORDER is itself a fingerprint, independent of the values.

js.$comment: Recorded. canvasSeed is derived from the profile id and held stable: real browsers return an identical canvas hash on every read, and randomising per read is itself the tell.
